In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Pleiades open cluster.
the determination of the mass–luminosity relation, and the mass–colour–luminosity relations for Pleiades and αPer stars.
the study of the properties and formation mechanisms of BDs and very low mass stars (VLMS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pleiades is a very active cluster with a high binary fraction.
the Pleiades BD population is not well represented by any of the models, and that the Praesepe BD population is not yet well understood.
the dust-free models are in reasonable agreement for the bulk of the Pleiades BD population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Pleiades is a very young cluster (τ∼ 100 Myr) where the dust-free Next-Gen isochrones are a good fit to the K, J−H, J−K and I−K CMD, but where the I−K colours are too red for stars in the range 0.1–0.2 M⊙.
the dust-free Next Gen models fit the data well for I− K∼ 1–3, but are too blue in H, K and J for I−K∽ 3.5.
the dust-free Next Gen model isochrones are a good fit to the CMDs of the Pleiades for I−K< 2.5 and the J−H and J−K diagrams for J−H> 1.1 and J−K> 1.2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pleiades BD population is not consistent with a single isochrone, and that the Pleiade BD sequence appears to be different from that of Praesepe.
the dust-free Next-Gen models provide a good fit to Pleiades BD data, but the dusty models are preferred for Praesepe BDs.

the NextGen models provide a good fit to the data for the Pleiades in the K, I, J−K, and J, J − K CMDs, and the dusty models provide a good description of the Praesepe data in the same CMDs, with the exception of the K, I − K CMD, where both sets of models are inconsistent with the data for I − K > 4.3.
